We’re really pleased to hear that you’ve noticed positive changes this year and that your recent experience using Patchs worked well, including being contacted so promptly after submitting your request.

It’s wonderful to hear that both you and your son felt well looked after by Laura. She will be delighted to know that you found her knowledgeable, professional and thorough. Feedback like yours means a great deal to the team, and it’s reassuring to know that your appointment left you feeling confident in the care you received.

Thank you again for your kind comments; we genuinely appreciate them. If you ever need anything further, please don’t hesitate to get in touch.

RESPONSE TO UPDATED REVIEW:

Thank you for taking the time to update your review, and I'm sorry to hear that your more recent experience did not match the positive one you described previously.

I'm sorry you felt the consultation on 4th March was not handled well, and I can understand how upsetting it must have been to feel unheard, particularly when you were already dealing with a health concern.

I do want to offer some reassurance that the advice given during your appointment was provided with your best interests in mind. Where a patient may have access to private healthcare, a clinician may sometimes suggest that as an option, not to dismiss your concerns, but as a genuine alternative that could get you seen more quickly. The GP who joined the consultation did so in order to offer a second opinion, and we are satisfied that the clinical advice given was sound. I appreciate that this may not have felt that way in the moment, and I'm sorry if the manner in which it was communicated left you feeling that way.

Regarding the phone number, I apologise that the local dialling code was not included. As a Chester practice, we sometimes omit the local dialling code, but I appreciate that's not helpful if you're unfamiliar with the area code.

To address the message that didn't reach you, it's worth knowing that messages from the practice are sent via the NHS App by default. If you have notifications enabled within the NHS App, it may have been delivered there. If a message fails to deliver through the app, it should automatically be resent as an SMS text after a short period of time. It may be worth checking your NHS App notifications in case it is sitting there.

Kind regards,
